clue.text: Painters include a Russian mystic

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, members of Britain's Royal Academy of painters
to include something is to put it in

explanation.surface: Some artists take a Russian holy man into their circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Grigori Rasputin was the mystic who held sway over the last Tsar's family; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasputin was the Siberian faith healer and holy man at the court of Nicholas II.

clue.text: Jolly good-or just sound?

explanation.surface: Is something very fine, or merely noisy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattling good' is an old British intensifier meaning very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattling means excellent, as in a rattling good yarn, and also making a clattering noise.

clue.text: Whereon Taurus grazes?

parts.note: Taurus is the bull among the constellations, so its pasture would be heavenly turf

explanation.definitionFit: A star-shaped flowering plant of the grass and lily families, imagined here as a constellation's pasture.

clue.text: No opening for dairy produce, says?

definitions.note: verb sense: voices or speaks, as in to utter words

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its opening

parts.note: butter is made in the dairy

explanation.surface: A dairy is unable to start making its butter, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No opening for' drops B from BUTTER. The definition 'says' stands for the bare verb 'say', a looseness of the period.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak or voice words is to utter them.

clue.text: Types of emphasis

parts.note: types here are printing type: the sloping kind used to stress words

explanation.definitionFit: Sloping print is the printer's usual way of stressing words.

clue.text: Good sorts of house-builders?

explanation.surface: Decent people are the ones who build our homes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brick' is old British slang for a reliable, good-natured person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependable friends are called bricks in British slang, and builders lay bricks to raise walls.

clue.text: Some character we might look up?

explanation.surface: A person of note whom we might admire.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'character' is a testimonial from an employer, and you look up a source or entry in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A testimonial for a job applicant is called a character; a source consulted in a book is one too.

clue.text: Scientist sees French priest about one

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A physicist goes to see a French priest about a single matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' is a link; Marie and Pierre Curie discovered radium.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Curie, pioneer of radioactivity, double Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Rich fabric for a mere sword-swallower /

explanation.surface: Luxurious cloth intended for a lake creature that gulps down blades.
explanation.walkthrough: In Arthurian legend an arm 'clothed in white samite' rises from the mere (lake) to catch Excalibur and draw it under.
explanation.definitionFit: Samite is a heavy silk woven with gold, worn by the Lady of the Lake's arm in Tennyson.

clue.text: Fish connected with soles ?

explanation.surface: Some fish are related to other flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Soles are fish too, which pulls 'connected' towards relatives; the second sense is the soles of boots fitted with blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Skates are flat rays, and boots with blades fixed under the feet for gliding on ice.

clue.text: As to replacing path, lay it before breakfast ?

indicators.note: the two words as to are placed again in a new order

parts.note: a path or trail is a track

explanation.surface: A gardener muses about relaying a path before the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' rearranges AS TO into TOAS. The definition reads 'lay' as setting the table: you put this holder of slices out before breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack for hot slices of bread is set on the table when laying it for the morning meal.

clue.text: Class, without high-class place for debate

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a school class is a form
U is the old British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A school group, short of anything upmarket, looks for somewhere to argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: FORM goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman public square where citizens gathered to argue, now any assembly for open discussion.

clue.text: Beer whose real gravity is altered

indicators.note: the letters are changed into another arrangement

parts.note: g is the physics symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: A brewer remarks that the true specific gravity of an ale has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is altered' rearranges REAL plus G; 'whose' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, bottom-fermented beer is a type of the drink.

clue.text: Cut off from pit centre, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A miner is isolated from the middle of the coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PIT CENTRE; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something on its way, as a pass or a message, is to cut it off.

clue.text: Pole can use different shades of meaning

parts.note: N is the north pole

indicators.note: different signals the letters made into something else

explanation.surface: A Polish speaker manages to employ subtle variations of sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the North Pole, N; 'different' turns CAN USE into UANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle differences in sense or tone between closely related words.

clue.text: Firm saw site for development along the shore

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the letters are developed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A company has seen a building plot by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for development' rearranges SAW SITE into ASTWISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Following the coast, as a ship sailing round rather than across the sea.

clue.text: One for the overtaking driver?

explanation.surface: A motorist asks for one thing when passing another car.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is a golfer: a single, one player going round alone, is often allowed to play through, overtaking slower groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means one; on a golf course a lone player is called a single and may pass a slower match.

clue.text: Putting on an early feature film?

definitions.text: Putting on an early feature film?

parts.words: Putting on an early feature film?
parts.note: not a cinema screening but a thin coat of soapsuds put on the face, a feature, first thing in the morning before shaving

explanation.definitionFit: Spreading shaving foam on the face early in the day covers the features with a soapy coat.

clue.text: USA's last to make such attacks

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new word

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: America's final move is to launch these offensives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges USA'S LAST; 'such' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent physical or military onslaughts.

clue.text: African soldier appears to demand backing of Republicans

parts.note: to demand is to ask

indicators.note: backing means the word is read from the back

parts.note: the IRA is the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: A soldier in Africa seems to call for support from Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing of' turns IRA round to ARI; 'appears to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An askari was a local soldier or policeman serving the colonial powers in East Africa.

clue.text: Egg is sound in our view

indicators.note: sound shows the phrase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: something in our view is in sight

explanation.surface: A breakfast egg looks perfect to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg' is the verb, as in egging someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg on is to urge or stir up someone to act.

clue.text: Flora's rings

parts.note: Flora, goddess of flowers, would have rings made of blooms and leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Circles of flowers and leaves woven together, the kind of ring a flower goddess wears.

clue.text: Literary squire's picture ?

explanation.surface: A portrait of a gentleman from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Squire Western is the hard-riding landowner in Fielding's Tom Jones; a 'picture' is a film, here a cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: Squire Western is Sophia's father in Tom Jones; a cowboy film is a genre of motion picture.

clue.text: Talks of southern summits

parts.note: summits are peaks

explanation.surface: Discussions about the mountains of the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Says words aloud, holds forth.

clue.text: What customers pay outside the Statute of Uses

indicators.note: outside means one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: customers pay the prices charged
a statute is an act of parliament

explanation.surface: A lawyer considers charges levied beyond an old Statute of Uses.
explanation.walkthrough: The Statute of Uses is a real 1535 English law, which makes 'Uses' look part of a title; it is the definition. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs or habitual ways of doing things are uses.

clue.text: Stop on deck

parts.note: the order to halt shouted by sailors aboard ship

explanation.definitionFit: A seafaring command meaning cease or hold, heard aboard ship.

clue.text: Raised a Dutch town

parts.note: to raise animals is to breed them, past tense bred

explanation.surface: Someone was brought up in a town in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Breda is a town in North Brabant in the south of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Distinctive mark of animal — no tail

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter, its tail

parts.note: a badger is a burrowing animal

explanation.surface: A creature is recognisable by its missing tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'no tail' drops R from BADGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem or token worn to show membership or rank.

clue.text: One periodical has a back view of a bird

indicators.note: a back view shows these pieces from behind, so they read right to left

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a magazine is a mag

explanation.surface: A single magazine features a picture of a bird from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back view of' reverses the whole run I MAG A; 'has' and 'of a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The agami is a South American trumpeter, a long-legged wading fowl.

clue.text: Take steps to get economists for routine drudgery

parts.note: to tread is to take steps
James Mill and his son John Stuart Mill were both economists, so the surname covers them

explanation.surface: Walking off to fetch the economists is just more tedious work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' and 'for' are links; the one name MILL stands for two economists, father and son.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill turned by walking, and figuratively any monotonous round of toil.

clue.text: Camp follower's poor result

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: a poor version of the word is a scrambled one

explanation.surface: Someone trailing an army gets a bad outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges RESULT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutler was a trader who followed an army and sold provisions to the soldiers.

clue.text: Reviles in Sam Weller's ways, say ?

indicators.note: say shows the words are taken as spoken

parts.note: Sam Weller in Dickens's Pickwick Papers says V for W, so ways comes out as vays

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the habits of a famous Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Weller, Mr Pickwick's Cockney servant, swaps W for V in his speech, so 'in ways' becomes 'in vays'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigh is to speak bitterly against, to rail at or abuse.
